plants.name: Chrysanthemum morifolium
plants.description: Dense, many-petaled blooms in gold, white, crimson and bronze crowd Japanese temple gardens and festival halls. Growers train single plants into cascading domes or hundreds of flowers on one stem.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn, roughly September through November, with late-blooming varieties peaking in late autumn
plants.location: Japan (gardens and chrysanthemum festivals across Honshu)
plants.funFact: A 16-petaled golden chrysanthemum is the emblem of Japan's Imperial family, and the flower is celebrated at an annual festival.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: Rows of trees turn whole suburbs lavender-blue, then carpet the pavements in fallen trumpet-shaped flowers. Each tree blooms in billowing clusters while the fern-like foliage is still sparse.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring, around October through November in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: Sydney university students nicknamed jacarandas 'exam trees' because the blossoms appear just as final exams begin.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: A glossy-leaved evergreen shrub that lights up the cooling autumn garden with delicate, open flowers. Its petals drop easily, scattering the ground with pink and white confetti.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn into early winter, commonly beginning in October or November and continuing through December or January
plants.location: Temperate gardens of Japan, the southeastern United States and mild-climate regions worldwide
plants.funFact: Sasanquas open months before the better-known spring camellias, giving gardens flowers when most plants are winding down.
